test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 29 Dec, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements is NOT true?

options.text: The total energy before and after the transformation always remains constant.
Energy can neither be created nor destroyed.
The total energy before and after the transformation is not constant.
Energy can only be transformed from one form to another.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Law of Conservation of Energy** states that energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed from one form to another.
 
• The **total energy** in a closed system remains constant before and after any transformation.
 
• When energy changes form, such as from kinetic to potential energy, the overall energy quantity remains unchanged.
 
• Option 3 is incorrect because it contradicts the conservation principle by stating that the total energy before and after the transformation is not constant.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **First Law of Thermodynamics:**

 
 
• This law is synonymous with the conservation of energy principle.
 
• It states that the total energy of an isolated system is constant; energy can be transformed from one form to another but cannot be created or destroyed.
 
 
 
• **Forms of Energy:**
 
 
• Energy exists in various forms such as kinetic, potential, thermal, chemical, electrical, and nuclear energy.
 
• These forms of energy can transform from one type to another but the total energy remains unchanged in a closed system.
 
 
 
• **Energy Transformation:**
 
 
• Examples include a roller coaster converting potential energy to kinetic energy and vice versa, or a battery converting chemical energy to electrical energy.
 
 
 
• **Closed System:**
 
 
• A closed system is one where no energy enters or leaves the system; the total energy within the system remains constant.
